summary: LinkedIn has two very different paths. Sign in with LinkedIn and posting as a member are self-serve once you have an app tied to a verified Company Page. Anything organizational (Pages, ads, analytics) is partner-gated, with no published review time, and individuals are likely rejected.
time_to_first_connection: Self-serve products: minutes to about an hour of clicking (inferred; docs state no review step)
time_to_production: Self-serve: no review step documented. Community Management API and other partner products: no official figure; two stages (Development then Standard tier) plus a screen recording and test credentials.
effort: Create a LinkedIn Page, create and verify the app with a Page super admin, add products. For org-level APIs: legal organization, business email, website, privacy policy, a separate new app, and a Standard-tier application.

approval.kind: None for self-serve products (OpenID Connect sign-in, Share on LinkedIn). Application and review for partner products (Advertising, Community Management, Lead Sync, Conversions, Matched Audiences). Sales Navigator for approved partners only; Compliance closed.
approval.who_reviews: LinkedIn partner/API review team; Page super admin for app verification
approval.stated_wait: No official figure. Restricted APIs are evaluated case by case with no fixed timeline.

steps.title: Create or have a LinkedIn Page (Company Page)
steps.detail: Quick Start lists creating a LinkedIn Page as step 1 for Marketing APIs. Evidence label: doc-stated (Marketing quick-start); for self-serve products the page requirement is doc-stated only by a secondary source (dev.to) -> unverified in official docs.

steps.title: Create app in Developer Portal
steps.detail: Go to /developers/apps/new. Associate the app with the Company Page. .

steps.title: Page admin verifies the app (app verification)
steps.detail: Developer generates a verification URL; a Page (super) admin approves it. Secondary source says instant if you are the admin yourself (label: unverified in official docs; official LinkedIn help page a1665329 could not be fetched, robots-blocked). CMA review doc-stated that a super admin of the Page must verify.

steps.title: Add self-serve products on Products tab
steps.detail: 'Sign in with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect' (scopes openid, profile, email) and 'Share on LinkedIn' (w_member_social). Docs say these are self-serve Open Permissions; docs do not state timing or any review step . Secondary source says tick box + accept terms, no queue.

steps.title: Register redirect URL on Auth tab; copy Client ID/Secret
steps.detail: Absolute HTTPS URL, no query params or fragment; must exactly match redirect_uri .

steps.title: Run 3-legged authorization code flow
steps.detail: Member must log in and consent in browser; auth code lasts 30 minutes . Token endpoint https://www.linkedin.com/oauth/v2/accessToken; userinfo https://api.linkedin.com/v2/userinfo; sub is pairwise per app.

steps.title: For partner-gated APIs: request product and complete access form
steps.detail: Products tab -> request Advertising API / Community Management API etc.; fill access form; Dev tier first, then separately apply for Standard tier (screen recording, test credentials, privacy policy).

requirements.text: A LinkedIn Page (Company Page) and a Page super admin to verify the app.
Community Management API: registered legal organization with a commercial use case, verified business email, website/domain and privacy policy.
HTTPS redirect URL with no query parameters or fragment, exactly matching redirect_uri.

composio.note: Composio can supply the OAuth app so you can start without registering one; users see 'Composio' on the consent screen, scopes are Composio's defaults, and rate-limit quota is shared. Register your own app (this guide) for production branding, custom scopes, a dedicated quota, faster polling, or private instances.

gotchas.text: Access tokens last 60 days (expires_in 5184000). Refresh tokens are NOT available to ordinary apps; programmatic refresh tokens only for approved Marketing Developer Platform partners (365-day fixed TTL, access token 60 days). Otherwise repeat the auth flow.
Programmatic refresh doc sample responses are internally inconsistent (86400 expires_in; minute-like values); check real responses.
Community Management API: only registered legal organizations with commercial use cases; personal email fails vetting; need verified business email, website/domain, privacy policy.
If CMA rejected you cannot reapply with the same app; must create a new app.

Development tier Community Management app must be a new app with no other API product; page posting therefore needs a separate app from Share/Sign-in app. Dev tier limits: 500 calls/app/day, 100/member/day. Must integrate within 12 months.
App name/logo cannot include LinkedIn or Microsoft names/logos (e.g. 'Linked', 'In').
Share on LinkedIn rate limits: 150 requests/member/day, 100,000/app/day; OIDC userinfo 500/member/day. Page metadata dates are old (2021/2023/2025) so verify in portal.
Changing scopes requires users to re-authenticate; requesting a different scope than previously granted invalidates earlier tokens.
LinkedIn may monitor and suspend access post-approval; may decline Standard upgrade even if minimums met.
Marketing API versions sunset regularly (202511 sunsets Nov 16, 2026); LinkedIn-Version header required for versioned APIs.

blockers.blocker: You want to post as a Company Page but are an individual or small team without a legal organization.
blockers.what_to_do: Org posting has no self-serve path. Post as the member via Share on LinkedIn instead.
You cannot reapply with the same app; create a new app and fix the stated gaps first.

blockers.blocker: No refresh tokens for ordinary apps (access tokens last 60 days).
blockers.what_to_do: Re-run the OAuth flow roughly every 60 days; programmatic refresh is only for approved Marketing Developer Platform partners.

blockers.blocker: Page super admin unavailable to verify your app.
blockers.what_to_do: Get a super admin of the associated Page to approve the verification link; an agent cannot do this for you.
